put_response.name: PAN-OS Allowed VNC TCP/5900 Activity
put_response.description: Detects allowed initial PAN-OS traffic from an internal source to TCP/5900, a port commonly associated with VNC remote-support software. The rule identifies repeated network activity; it does not prove that a VNC session was established, that anyone authenticated, or that the destination was compromised.
put_response.note:
## What this alert means

An internal system made at least three allowed initial TCP/5900 connections to the same destination within five minutes. TCP/5900 is commonly used by VNC remote-support software. The alert shows allowed network traffic, not a successful VNC session or compromise.

## What to check

Review the source and destination addresses, their system owners, the connection time, firewall action, and any related PAN-OS rule. Confirm whether the activity is approved remote support or administration. Check whether the connections were repeated, whether authentication succeeded on the destination, and whether related threat or endpoint alerts exist.

## Response

Do not automatically block, isolate, reset passwords, or disable accounts based on this alert alone. If the activity is not authorised or successful access cannot be explained, preserve the relevant logs, contact the source and destination owners, and escalate through the approved incident-response process.
author: SOC Analyst
put_response.query: event.dataset:"panw.panos" and panw.panos.type:"TRAFFIC" and network.transport:tcp and destination.port:5900 and panw.panos.action:allow and event.action:flow_started and source.ip:(10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12 or 192.168.0.0/16)
